description: This course introduces a thorough understanding of structural members and their strength, stiffness, and stability, and develops the capability to solve practical engineering problems involving stress and strain analysis in elementary structural members, such as bars and beams. The learning objectives are: to learn about the simple and compound stresses at a point in a material and its evaluation; to understand the concept of strain energies that forms the basis of analysis in many cases; to know about the shear forces, bending moments, bending stresses and shear stresses in a beam; to study various methods to find the deflection of beams under various load conditions; and to study the various theories of failure of materials.

syllabus.title: Simple and Compound Stress and Strain
syllabus.body: Simple Stress and Strain: Mechanical Properties of Materials, Concept of stress and strain, various type of stresses, stress-strain diagrams, composite sections, Thermal stresses, strain analysis, relation between elastic constants. Compound Stress and Strain: Principal stresses and principal planes, Mohr's stress circle, Principal strains, Mohr's strain circle, Relation between principal stresses and principal strains.

syllabus.title: Shear Force and Bending Moment Diagrams; Strain Energies
syllabus.body: Shear Force and Bending Moment Diagrams: Shear force and bending moment diagrams for various types of loading and supports, Point of contra flexure, Loading and bending moment diagrams from shear force diagrams. Centroid and Moment of Inertia: Centroid of laminas of various shapes, Moment of inertia of laminas of different shapes. Strain Energies: Resilience, strain energy due to various types of loading.

syllabus.title: Bending and Shear Stress in Beams
syllabus.body: Bending Stress in Beams: Stresses due to simple bending, Composite or Flitched beams, combined direct and bending stress. Shear Stress in Beams: Shear stress distribution, Variation of shear stress in beams of various sections

syllabus.title: Slope and Deflection; Theories of Failure
syllabus.body: Slope and Deflection: Slope and deflection at a point using different methods, deflection of beams due to shear stress. Theories of Failure: Different theories of failure, Significance, graphical representation.

outcomes: Determine the values of stresses in materials
Draw shear force and bending moment diagrams
Find shear and bending stresses in beams
Find slope and deflection of beams
textbooks: G H Ryder, "Strength of Materials", ELBS, 3rd edition, 1969
S S Rattan, "Strength of Materials", Tata McGraw Hill, India, 3rd Edition, 2017

Popov E P, "Engineering Mechanics of Solids", Prentice Hall of India, New Delhi, 2nd edition, 1999.
